description: Bounds of the drop cap candidate signal. A drop cap is an oversized initial standing at the head of a piece of running text, and it is found here from three general typographic facts and no publication specific one. 'min_first_run_size_ratio' is how large the paragraph's first style run must be against that paragraph's own median character size: an initial set three lines tall is several times the body size, while a paragraph opening in small caps or bold is barely above it. 'max_first_run_chars' is how many non-space characters that run may carry, which is what separates an initial from a heading or a lead-in phrase that happens to be set larger. 'max_body_rank_in_article' is how far into its article the paragraph may stand, counted over the body text paragraphs of that article in page order; a paragraph on the page its article opens on qualifies whatever its rank, because that is where a piece's opening initial goes. The three corpus drop caps stand at ranks 3, 5 and 5, so the bound is set at the deepest of them and holds each of them without relying on the opening page rule. 'excerpt_chars' bounds the opening of the paragraph quoted into the review draft, which is what a human reads to recognise the paragraph; it steers no decision.
